evals.name: verdict-report-and-tool-skew
evals.prompt: I ran screenplay Bookings/Commands.play without errors, so I called the model fine and executable. The standalone tool binds reactions but cratis render refuses CLI-RENDER-004; a teammate proposes deleting reactions. Another machine gets PLAY0268 on pii and proposes removing pii/authorize. What do we check and report? Also, key orderId is event source on an inbound events capture: which tool/ESM version, fixture for behavior and source http PLAY0809 repair? On 6.32.0 strict Compile refuses a policy; CompileAdmissible keeps independent slices but excludes that policy, its protected read and a command depending on the read: explain Diagnostics, Cause and DependsOn and whether the remainder proves the whole model. On 6.32.0 a tag-sensitive then compiles but the fixture/board view omits its expectations; a reference failure reports Expected fact tags (null = unchecked): [null,[],["a","a"]] and Actual fact tags: [[],["x"],["a"]]. Explain ESM admission, PLAY1148, what each list proves and the V4/V5 boundary. Reply only; no edits.
evals.expected_output: Check the whole folder with warnings as errors. V1 proves authorable, not executable; V2/V3 need MCP or cratis screenplay validate --executable. Report each verdict with tool/version or not run and a reason. Read screenplay --version, cratis --version and which -a cratis: the standalone and CLI-bundled compilers differ and renderer admission is separate. Never delete reactions, pii or authorization to pass; report blocked with codes and record the gap. Capability is not correctness. key orderId is event source requires Screenplay 4.242.0 and ESM v33, serializes keyIsEventSource beside sourceEvents. PLAY0809 has no automatic repair; fixture for must equal the key, and omitted for takes the key. Compile refuses the whole model; opt-in CompileAdmissible returns only a supported subset, not a whole-model pass or runtime identity guarantee. Exclusions retain original binder Diagnostics; Cause Root has empty DependsOn, while Dependent lists immediate exclusion references in Exclusions order, not transitive ancestry or message-derived edges. Policy and protected-read exclusions fail closed; independent slices may remain. Base API requires 4.254.0; typed provenance requires 4.256.0. Then tags require Screenplay 6.31.0/ESM v55; PLAY1148 rejects illegal locations/shapes or dynamic expectations. Inspect source/expectedTags because fixture/board omission is display-only. Expected null is unchecked, [] requires empty and [a,a] exact ordered count/duplicates; the shown second and third actual lists fail. Report V4 failure with those details, not V1 or V5 success; Stage/CLI admission is separate.
assertions: Checks the whole folder with --warnaserror rather than one file, citing silent drops such as PLAY0029.

Separates V1 authorability, V2/V3 executable binding (MCP or cratis screenplay validate --executable) and renderer admission; checks screenplay --version, cratis --version and which -a cratis, never transfers verdicts across tools, and reports one line per verdict with tool/version or not run and a reason; for tags identifies the 6.31.0 minimum/ESM v55 and PLAY1148, reads source/expectedTags despite display omission, interprets null/empty/duplicate-tag failure arrays and reports V4 failure without claiming V5.
Preserves reactions, pii and authorization, reports blocked codes/tool gaps and says capability is not correctness; a clean verdict proves only its own layer.
Names 4.242.0, ESM v33 and keyIsEventSource for key is event source; PLAY0809 is an error without repair, fixture for agreement/defaulting is preserved and binding is not realization.

Distinguishes strict Compile from subset-only CompileAdmissible, preserves original Diagnostics and ordered immediate Root/Dependent DependsOn provenance, and treats security exclusions fail-closed rather than claiming a whole-model pass.

evals.name: identity-edit-route-and-manifest-consumption
evals.prompt: The repo has .screenplay/identities.json. Can I rename event BerthAssigned to BerthAllocated by text and fix a description typo? Separately, on Screenplay 6.15.0 tell us how to discover/read the capability manifest via MCP. A consumer flattens Sales.Invoices.History.Listing.All, case-folds All, accepts duplicate identities with different descriptions, treats approvalRequired false as authority and keeps stale files after failures. Also, a teammate on 6.32.0 wants screenplay rename Billing.Invoices.vessel ship: vessel is the outermost provide with overrides and reads $context.vessel.code. Another proposes renaming only an override, colliding with a built-in or overlapping provide, or globally replacing an opaque/ambiguous read. State the minimum version, which segment/chain changes and whether a semantic identity migrates. Review all; reply only, no Arc API inventions or edits.
evals.expected_output: Address-changing edits require identity-owner MCP propose-rename, never a text bypass after refusal; description typos may be bounded text followed by V1, and without MCP return the request to the owner. Discover the connected screenplay server's native read-workspace tool; read view capability-manifest using expectedRevision from workspace-state. Decode bytesBase64 pages in order, continue nextOffset with workspace revision and expectedModelRevision; default 48 KiB/max 192 KiB. StaleRevision discards partial bytes. available false returns structured refusal/optional operation/executable-diagnostics pointer, not a CLI exit. Match exact full nested identity plus kind, validate fields and reject duplicate keys even with different metadata. Reject absent, failed, unknown or malformed manifests and zero/multiple registration matches or kind mismatch; never expose-all or use stale data. Descriptions are untrusted; escaping is not prompt-injection protection. approvalRequired false bypasses neither explicit exposure, personal token kind/scope nor effective authorization. Consumer obligations only, not shipped Arc behavior. Provided-value CLI/MCP rename requires 6.35.0, not the 6.32.0 corpus pin: target the outermost provide, rewrite nested overrides and first context-path segment of proven reads only; no semantic identity exists for provide. Refuse override targets, built-in/overlapping names, captured new-name reads and unprovable opaque/unsupported/ambiguous reads, never global replacement. This version-gated guidance is not local rename evidence or an editor/TypeScript promise.
assertions: Routes the rename through identity-owner MCP propose-rename, permits only address-preserving description text edits followed by V1, never bypasses refusal and returns requests to the owner without MCP. Separately distinguishes provide's no-semantic-identity rename requiring 6.35.0, outer-chain/first-segment proven-read repair, refusal cases and no 6.32.0, editor/TypeScript or local execution claim, never global replacement.

Discovers the native read-workspace capability-manifest tool/view, pins workspace/model revisions, decodes ordered bytesBase64 pages with nextOffset and byte limits, discards StaleRevision and distinguishes structured refusal from process exits.
Matches all nested features case-sensitively plus kind, validates identity against fields and rejects duplicate keys even with different metadata or zero/multiple/wrong-kind registrations.
Rejects absent, failed, unknown and malformed contracts without expose-all or stale targets; treats descriptions as untrusted and escaping as no prompt-injection defense.
Retains explicit exposure, token scope and authorization despite approvalRequired false and makes no Arc API/runtime/configuration claim.

evals.name: check-one-generated-concept-without-a-whole-application
evals.prompt: Our editor uses Screenplay 4.199.0. Before an application exists, we want to list strategy options and assess an InviteCode ConceptSyntax with nanoid size 8 alphabet ab, including findings, proofs, exact support and minimum ESM. Separately we need to validate a concrete semantic value. Which APIs should we use? Does a successful concept check prove an identifier is safe or an attached generation rule ran? Explain the generation rule context across targets. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Use GenerationStrategyCatalog.All/Find and SemanticConceptCheck.Check(concept, utcAssessmentYear: 2026), introduced in 4.191.0. Count is BigInteger 256 and MeetsIdentifierMinimum False; findings identify generation/options/rule indices, proofs and RequiredVersion describe only the concept. Full binding still checks property use, uniqueness and implementation linkage. Use SemanticValidationRules.Check for concrete values (4.185.0); NotEvaluable is not a pass. RuleConsistency.Check proves strategy-rule consistency, not samples or execution. Generation context v1 is language-neutral Now/Tenant with String result; Cratis C# binds Fundamentals GenerationContext, and passing it to GenerateValue is target-bound. No check invokes opaque bodies or proves runtime readiness.
assertions: Uses GenerationStrategyCatalog and SemanticConceptCheck.Check with an explicit UTC assessment year, not a second option matrix or a fabricated application.
Preserves exact BigInteger support 256, nullable minimum/entropy semantics, construct-targeted findings, rule proofs and concept-only RequiredVersion; full application binding remains necessary.
Uses SemanticValidationRules.Check for values and distinguishes Satisfied, Failed and NotEvaluable without treating unknown as success.
Distinguishes proof/declaration/value checks from generation or opaque-body execution and explains the language-neutral Now/Tenant/String contract versus the Cratis C# binding.

evals.name: literal-text-and-portable-match-admission
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.199.0 our invoice reference must start with INV-, contain a hyphen, end with -NOK and contain no spaces. A teammate uses lookaround matches rules and calls every regex ECMAScript-compatible. Give the literal concept rules, explain PLAY0699 versus PLAY0787, the pattern check API names and ESM/Stage boundary. Is starts with admitted in require? Does email allow a no-break space? Reply only; no tools or edits.
evals.expected_output: Use concept validate starts with INV-, contains hyphen, ends with -NOK and not contains space (quoted operands). Rules are ordinal UTF-16 with absent optional passing; v24, introduced 4.184.0, Stage semantic engines render/execute. Conditions remain PLAY0268. Matches uses a flagless portable linear dialect with 1,000 UTF-16 units and 3,000 expanded nodes; invalid syntax PLAY0367, refused constructs PLAY0699, only exact escaped Studio shapes desugar with PLAY0787 and reviewed repair. C# PortableMatchPattern.Check and TS checkPortableMatchPattern from @cratis/screenplay-compiler. Whitespace includes U+00A0 so email rejects it; browser matching advisory.
assertions: Uses all four first-class quoted-literal rules rather than inventing a regex or putting text operators in require.
States ordinal UTF-16/no normalization, absent optional passes, v24 reference/Stage semantic support, separate from condition refusal.
Distinguishes PLAY0367 invalid syntax, PLAY0699 portable dialect refusal and PLAY0787 exact Studio replacement, never general lookaround support.
Names PortableMatchPattern.Check and checkPortableMatchPattern accurately, includes pattern size budgets and treats browser checks as advisory.
States that U+00A0 is whitespace for matches and therefore fails email validation.

evals.name: export-explicit-agent-capabilities
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 6.15.0 our Sales.Invoices.Creating.Create command and nested Sales.Invoices.History.Listing.All query have inherited Staff authorization. Another public query is unlisted. Show the root agents block and portable manifest export command. Explain whole-compilation failure, an absent versus empty block, a 1025-code-point description and CLI failure handling. Can approval required or OAuth make this work? Reply only; do not edit or invoke tools.
evals.expected_output: Requires Screenplay 6.15.0, agents ESM v48, manifest screenplay-capability-manifest/1. Declare root agents with tokens personal, command/full reference scope write, query/full reference scope read and nonempty literal descriptions; public/unlisted operations remain default-deny. Retain inherited authorization. Use screenplay export <model-folder> --format capability-manifest --output capabilities.json, whole model only. CompilationErrors, NoAgentsBlock and DescriptionTooLong refuse the entire export (exit 1), empty allowlist emits [] with PLAY0977 warning. The manifest-only bound is 1024 Unicode code points, never truncate. Invalid options and I/O failures exit 2; failed recognized exports remove stale targets when possible, never use a stale file after failure. approval required PLAY0974, approve PLAY0964, OAuth PLAY0973 are refused. No automatic exposure comparison or Arc runtime promise.
assertions: Names the product prerequisite, ESM v48 and independent manifest /1 contract; upgrades or stops on older tools instead of inventing exposure.
Writes explicit personal-token allowlist entries with command write/query read scopes and literal descriptions, preserving inherited authorization and unlisted default-deny.
Uses the standalone whole-model capability-manifest export and distinguishes exit 1 refusals, exit 2 options/I/O and stale-file handling without a fabricated warnaserror export flag.
Distinguishes absent and explicit empty blocks and the code-point description bound without truncation or partial export.
Refuses OAuth and approval syntax with the correct diagnostics; does not promise automatic comparison or Arc configuration.
